headline: Evidence Over Hype
thesis: With AI adoption still outrunning proof, education leaders are turning to learning science, security hygiene and shared standards to decide what actually earns a place in schools.
summary: The through-line today is evidence before adoption. Inside Higher Ed's Educause 2026 coverage reports that deciding where AI adds real value is the number-one 2027 priority for campus tech leaders, while an Instructure analysis finds the most popular AI tool didn't crack the top 100 LTI tools and only about 11% of instructors have comprehensive AI training. THE Journal and Inside Higher Ed both published opinion pieces arguing that learning science should guide AI use decisions, and EdSurge asks whether schools are rewarding polished AI output over curiosity. On the infrastructure side, 1EdTech announced a 16-organization learner-mobility alliance after its Technical Congress and is retiring LTI 1.1 by October 2027, Ed-Fi's v6.1 standard adds a special-education data domain, and security reporting shows attackers impersonating IT staff on Teams.
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · October 22, 2026 · Caveat: sources were researched via web search only (direct site fetches not used), so some items are recent or evergreen rather than strictly same-day and dates reflect search-reported values.
